paper_summary: A short research note describing production of an aluminium matrix syntactic foam by thixoinfiltration: fly-ash-derived hollow ceramic micro-balloons (5 wt% relative to the aluminium) were placed between two Al-5052 alloy discs and infiltrated at 644 C (78.14% liquid fraction) with a hydraulic press force limited to 5 kN. Optical/SEM microscopy showed homogeneous balloon dispersion and good matrix-balloon anchorage; image binarisation gave ~45% porosity and an approximate density of 1.8 g/cm3, a ~30% density reduction versus the aluminium matrix. Vickers microhardness in the foam region rose to 70-75 HV100 versus 63-67 HV100 for the laminate and 60 HV100 for the thixoformed material.

records.sample_label: Al-5052 / Fly Ash syntactic foam (thixoinfiltrated, 5 wt% balloons)

processing.matrix_name: Commercial aluminium alloy Al 5052 (1.882 wt% Mg, 0.309 Fe, 0.171 Cr, 0.12 Si, balance Al)
processing.particle_grade: Fly ash hollow ceramic micro-balloons, 100 grit sieve fraction

structure.microstructure_notes: Image-J binarisation of optical micrographs gave an average porosity of 45% and an approximate density of 1.8 g/cm3 (~30% density reduction vs the Al matrix). Homogeneous balloon distribution, total anchorage, no defects at balloon-matrix interface. Balloon mean dimensions A (length) 266.185 um and B (width) 197.745 um with 2.5 um wall thickness; fly-ash balloon density stated as 0.6-0.8 g/cm3. Infiltration force limited to 5 kN to avoid balloon collapse.

test.specimen_notes: Vickers microhardness with 100 gf preload; foam region 70, 75, 75 HV100 vs 63/65/67 HV100 laminate and 60 HV100 thixoformed. Hardness is not a schema field, so no property value is filled. Compression tests of cellular materials are mentioned but no stress/modulus values are reported.

evidence.quote: In a steel mold machined for the procedure, two aluminum alloy discs were positioned, and a 5% by weight portion, relative to the aluminum portion, of Fly Ash balloons between these discs.

By analyzing the images using Image J software, using the binarization tool it was possible to determine the average porosity and to calculate the approximate value of the obtained density 45% and 1.8g/cm3.
The assembly was baked at a heating rate of 5°C/min until it reached a working temperature of 644°C ... the infiltration force was limited to 5 kN to prevent balloon collapse during the process.

extraction_notes: Very short (3-page) note with almost no quantitative mechanical data. Only one material condition is reported, so one record. Reported quantities: 5 wt% balloon loading, 644 C processing temperature, 1.8 g/cm3 density, ~45% porosity, ~30% density reduction. No modulus, strength, strain or energy values are given anywhere (the abstract mentions standardized compression tests but no results are shown), so all Properties fields are null. Vickers hardness (63-75 HV100, Table 2) has no schema field and is recorded in specimen_notes only. The 45% 'average porosity' from image binarisation is the total hollow/pore area including the balloon interiors, not unintended matrix porosity, so matrix_porosity_fraction was left null and the value placed in microstructure_notes. Balloon true density is given only as a range (0.6-0.8 g/cm3) so it was left null. Balloon size is reported as two orthogonal dimensions (266.185 um length, 197.745 um width) rather than a mean diameter, and the radius ratio eta is not stated (only a 2.5 um wall thickness), so both fields were left null rather than derived. Test temperature assumed room temperature (25 C) for the hardness test.
